title: Fix what the S1 phase code review found on the writer-session path
description: Bugfix phase after P131 (S1). The tasks run in series because three of them edit drive-phase.py. Lows from the same review are carried with BUG-29-dau (register F778).
desiredOutcome: The four high and medium findings of the S1 phase code review (F774-F777) are fixed red-first, so the writer-session path that the stage 1 measurement exercises has no known defect and 3.6.0 is not held by them.

findings.issue: review_fix now returns the reviewFixes entry for every writer dispatch of the task for as long as the entry exists, and finish_task (KEPT_AT_TASK_CLOSE) now keeps that entry past the task's close. Before, the one-shot 'dispatched' flag ended the injection. The entry is only removed by resolve_fixed (all findings withdrawn) or replaced by a new hand_back. So a later, unrelated writer dispatch of the same task, for example after a manual /audit:task reopen once the fix has closed at a new commit with a finding not yet withdrawn, takes the old findings and the REVIEW_FIX_HEAD preamble, and is forced to a fresh session by the non-empty 'dispatched' list. Nothing in the diff separates a retry or brief re-issue of the hand-back round (wanted) from a later re-open (not wanted). The new tests cover only the retry.
findings.resolution: Bound the entry to the round it was written for. For example, have review_fix return None once task.commit is set and differs from fix['from'] (the hand-back guard already reads 'from' this way), or record the start that closed the fix in finish_task, and add a case: a fix closed at a new commit, the task re-opened by hand, and the next dispatch carries the plain brief.

findings.issue: With the 'writer' mark and reviewFixes kept, a task-scoped drive over a writer task never reaches the 'drop the state when nothing else is in it' branch. The state file now stays until a phase-level finish drops it. The docstring says so, but no case covers a task-scoped drive that is never followed by a phase drive (rw4 covers only a task with no writer record).
findings.resolution: Either state in the docstring or the PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE section that a task-scoped run of a writer task leaves its state file behind by design, or drop the state when the kept marks hold no re-opened entry and the task was never handed back.

findings.issue: The guide says a gap at a green gate is `clauses-uncovered-writer` and 'once the rounds are spent it is the plain `clauses-uncovered`'. After this diff the plain decision is also asked when executor.writerModel is unset or does not read whole (writer_path_on), and the same holds for red-refused. The module docstring was updated for this (drive-phase.py:227-230) but the guide section that documents the same decision was not. The executor's outcome notes this and leaves it.
findings.resolution: Add 'or with executor.writerModel no longer set' to that sentence in PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, matching the module docstring.

tasks.title: A task re-opened by the phase-review hand-back is judged on its own work: clause coverage reads the diff against the commit it carried, its findings reach every re-dispatch, and the record survives the task's close
tasks.description: Register F774 (from the S1 phase code review). (1, high) diff_paths (drive-phase.py ~2473) lists only changes against HEAD, which already holds the re-opened task's first commit, so every clause the first commit delivered is path-not-in-diff (~2810) and the task can never pass clause coverage. For a re-opened start, read the changed paths against the commit the task carried (reviewFixes from / the journal's task.reopen record), so a clause cited to a file the first commit delivered still counts. (2, med) reviewFixes[tid].dispatched is keyed by task, not by start (~6092, ~1710): any re-dispatch after the first (retry, stale-brief re-issue) gets the plain brief without the confirmed findings - key it by start. (6, low) finish_task (~6738) pops reviewFixes and the writer record, losing the closed-at-no-new-commit guard and the warm session - keep them until the phase signs off.

add: tests/test_drive_phase.py: a re-opened task whose fix touches a.py only, with clauses cited to b.py from its first commit, passes clause coverage; a retry after the first fix dispatch still carries the confirmed findings in the prompt; and after a task-scoped drive closes the task, the hand-back's from-commit and the warm session are still found

outcome.technical: drive-phase.py: (1) new carried_paths(ctx, phase, task, tree) reads the commits the task carried off the journal's task.reopen rows (reopen_record) and lists each one's paths with git diff-tree --root -r -z --name-only, spelled as diff_paths spells them, plan records excluded; file_writer_return checks clause coverage against diff_paths union carried_paths, stops loudly when the journal or git cannot say; the filed diffPaths stays this start's diff. (2) reviewFixes[tid].dispatched is now the list of start keys whose dispatch carried the findings (hand_back writes []; legacy true reads as one dispatch via _fix_dispatched); review_fix returns the entry for every dispatch while the hand-back stands, so a retry (new start) or a stale-brief re-issue carries the findings; only the first dispatch may resume the warm session, later ones start fresh with brief + findings. (3) finish_task keeps KEPT_AT_TASK_CLOSE = (reviewFixes, writer) marks until the phase's finish drops the state; other marks still dropped and an empty state still removed. tests/test_drive_phase.py: new stage rw-block (_reopened_writer_cases, _reopened_finish_cases, fixture _rw_handed_back). Runs: stage rw-block 5/5 after the fix; gate python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_drive_phase.py exit 0, 512 cases; ruff check and vermin -t=3.8- on both files exit 0. Committed throwaway copy (/tmp/p1321-copy.Kxnh, git archive HEAD + working-tree diff, committed): python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py -> 192/194 files ok, the two red being tools/check-example-ledgers.py (fixedIn commits unresolvable in a history-less copy) and tools/measure-context.py, both allowed by the brief. Mutations in a second copy (/tmp/p1321-mut.7bXq, pycache purged each time, anchor count asserted 1): M1 carried_paths -> git ls-files (over-fire): rw0, rw1 red; M2 finish_task keeps every mark: rw3, rw4 red; M3 every fix dispatch resumes warm: rw2 red; each restored (diff -q vs project file: identical). Dependants: tests/test_drive_phase.py - changed, new stage added, all 512 cases green. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md - still correct: its finish_task line (dt cases) states the done print, not state removal; its _clause_coverage section says check reads 'whether the cited path changed', still true with the carried commit's paths passed as changed; no edit (outside files scope). README.md, docs/research/pipeline-cost-design.md, docs/research/pipeline-cost-levers.md - still correct: grep for reviewFixes/finish_task/diff_paths/clause coverage finds no statement about these paths ('hand-back' there is the subagent hand-back). plugins/audit/hooks/detect-plan-skip.py, governance/record-risk-confirmation.py, governance/stamp-verification.py, manifest/_areas.py - still correct: they reference drive-phase.py by basename and none reads reviewFixes, the writer mark or finish_task; no exported name was renamed or removed (diff_paths, review_fix, hand_back, finish_task keep their signatures). .github/sweep-costs.json, tests/test__runner_output.py, tests/test_run_test_gate.py, tools/sweep-selftests.py - still correct: whole-sweep run on the committed copy green for each; the sweep cost entry for the file is unchanged (one new stage, timing recorded run 196.3s, within its timeout).
outcome.descriptive: A task the phase review hands back is judged on its own work: clauses its first commit delivered still count, every re-dispatch carries the confirmed findings, and a task-scoped close keeps the hand-back record and warm session

tasks.description: Register F775. (3, med) redispatch (drive-phase.py ~4711) calls dispatch without the member's tree; since the reviewer runs as a session, a wave member's reviewer reads the phase tree without the member's work and open_dispatch records the wrong HEAD - take the tree from state.wave.trees as the resume branch (~4645) already does. (4, low-med) with executor.writerModel unset, resume on red-refused-writer / clauses-uncovered-writer stops with 'answer retry', which those decisions do not offer, and the next next re-raises the decision (~2100-2103, answers ~691/695) - offer retry on those two decisions when the writer path is off, or name what works. (5, low) cap_note (~2355) says 'still red after its resume rounds' though clause and red-first rounds spend the same budget - say what spent them.

tasks.title: Every reader of a fix task's red-first obligation asks one predicate, so a comment-only fix in a source file is not refused for lacking a test command
tasks.description: Register F776. audit-task.py _expects_red_first (~3082) writes expectRedFirst=false for a tdd fix task with an empty tests.add, but submit (drive-phase.py ~7274-7279), the executor brief (audit-lookup.py ~1057-1066) and the fix prompt (drive-phase.py ~6130) still decide on tests.mode and refuse a submit without a test command. Make the stored expectRedFirst (written only by _expects_red_first) the one thing every reader asks; a task with expectRedFirst false files red-first not-attempted with the reason and needs no command after --.

add: tests/test_drive_phase.py: a tdd fix task with expectRedFirst false and no tests.add submits with no command after -- and files red-first not-attempted naming why, while a tdd task with expectRedFirst true is still refused without one; and tests/test_audit_lookup.py: the executor brief for the first asks for no test command

tasks.title: The writer prompt names browser gates only from the plugin's own repository or the project's config, never from a file name a user project may also use
tasks.description: Register F777. audit-lookup.py ~810 BROWSER_GATE_SCRIPTS = ('capture-screenshots.mjs','check-report-interactive.mjs','verify.sh') (used ~890): in a user's project whose gate is ./scripts/verify.sh the writer is told not to run it because 'the drive runs the browser gates itself', so it never runs its own gate; npx playwright test gets the same sentence, a promise nothing in the drive keeps. Read the set from a config key (default empty; this repository's own config sets its three), add the key to the config schema and _config_rules, and word the sentence as what is true: the named commands are left to the phase gate.

add: tests/test_audit_lookup.py: on a fixture project whose gate is ./scripts/verify.sh and no config key, the writer prompt lists that command to run and says nothing about browser gates, while with the key naming it the command is left to the phase gate in those words; and tests/test__config_rules.py: the new key validates and an unknown value is reported

tasks.title: The release tier is green again on Windows and the spaced-path leg: the dev-module walk is rooted at the repo it is asked about, git fixtures are removed with the read-only-aware helper, and the miss-rate tool's command line quotes its interpreter
tasks.description: Release-tier CI run 39692464240 (ci/P131 @1c5ac5e0) went red on six jobs that were green on 3.5.0, from three S1 regressions (diagnosed from the job logs): (1) tools/lints/_output_lints.py ~2214-2218 suite_elsewhere_paths walks DEV_DIRS/DEV_FILES absolute under REPO_ROOT and relpaths them against a fixture repo_root - ValueError across drives on Windows (d0, e2e windows, windows plain/cp1252 2), wrong ../ paths silently on posix; root the walk at the repo asked about. (2) tests/test__output.py ~333-345 (mv11) and tests/test__output_lints.py ~1646-1675 (pn37/pn38) remove git fixtures with shutil.rmtree(ignore_errors=True), which cannot unlink git's read-only objects on Windows, so the fixture survives and the sweep's watched TMPDIR reports it; use _harness.remove_tree, and fix EVERY rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True) around a git fixture in tests/ and tools/ (grep the class, list each site). (3) tools/measure-affected-miss.py m15 (~1205-1210) builds '%s %s' % (sys.executable, ...) unquoted and the tool shlex.splits it (~743-745): backslashes eaten on Windows, a spaced interpreter split on the stress leg; quote with shlex.quote. After landing, the orchestrator re-dispatches the release tier.

add: tools/sweep-selftests.py: d0 asserts tools/lints/_not_swept.py is not in the nested set of a fixture repository rooted outside REPO_ROOT, red on today's code on posix too; and tools/measure-affected-miss.py: m15 builds its command lines with shlex.quote so an interpreter path holding a backslash or a space survives the split
